_comment: Day 6 electrical parameter rules, fixed 17 Nov 2026 BEFORE any Pakistan solve and before computing any model quantity that a holdout uses. Rationale and sources in day6/parameter_rules.md. Change only with a dated note there; after the first AC solve any change is post hoc.

lines._source: Per-circuit 50 Hz values from the research report table (reports/Pakistan grid model data.md, 6 Nov 2026): datasheet R_ac at 75 C, GMR and diameter with assumed geometry. Ratings from TSEP 2024-34 contingency tables (flow / rating = printed %).

500.rate_note: TSEP Table 5-2: 500 kV Gujranwala-N. Jhelum 1,500 MVA (stability-limited planning rating); datasheet thermal about 2,830

220.rate_note: research table value (TSEP Mardan-Tarbela 250 MVA); TSEP Sibbi-Quetta is 300 MVA

132.rate_note: TSEP Tables 5-2/5-4: 23 of 36 reconciling 132 kV rows are 112 MVA; others 182/184/202

66.rate_note: Lynx 490 A (the current behind 112 MVA at 132 kV) at 66 kV; assumption

lines.parallel_circuits: a branch with n circuits gets r/n, x/n, b*n, rate*n
lines.pi_model: exact (hyperbolic) equivalent pi for every line

line_sensitivity_variants._comment: Reported only; never replace the scored parameters.

transformers._comment: One equivalent branch per voltage pair per station (the builder's stubs). Capacity from PSS 44th Tables 2.16/2.17 (June 2019) where the station is S3-assigned (any tier), else the default. x on own base; R = X / xr_ratio.
transformers.pss_unit_split: PSS units of 450/600/750 MVA belong to the 500/220 kV pair; units of 160/250/320 MVA to the 220/132 kV pair of the same station

500-220.source: TSEP standard unit 750 MVA, two units initially; %X midpoint of 7.5-12 % range in research notes

220-132.source: TSEP standard unit 250 MVA; pandapower 220/110 kV 12 %

132-110.source: assumption; one odd OSM 110 kV tag

shunts._comment: Totals are TSEP inputs I4 (Tables 5-1 and 5-10). Reactors placed now; capacitors placed on Day 8 by the rule below (they need bus loads).
shunts.mvar_convention: Totals are NAMEPLATE MVAr at 1.0 pu voltage (PowerModels bs). TSEP's PSS/E summaries report MVAr at solved voltages (500 kV winter 1.035-1.056 pu), so delivered MVAr will differ by roughly V^2. Delivered MVAr is reported after the solve and is never iterated to match TSEP.
shunts.reactor_fixed_rule: Place each Table 5-9 reactor at the bus of its S3-assigned station (any tier) at that voltage. If there is none, its MVAr joins the proportional pool, so the snapshot total is unchanged.
shunts.reactor_pool_rule: The rest of each snapshot total goes to 500 kV buses of real stations (substation, plant, converter) in the main component, in proportion to half the total charging of the 500 kV circuits incident to the bus (each line end takes half its charging). Same placement shape in both snapshots, scaled to each total.
shunts.capacitor_rule: Day 8: 132 kV load buses, in proportion to bus reactive load, scaled to each snapshot total (continuous MVAr; the 2 x 48 MVAr bank size is noted, not imposed).

winter_openings._comment: TSEP Table 5-7 (PDF p.65): circuits opened in the winter peak and off-peak cases. Applied to the winter off-peak snapshot only. Each is mapped to model branches by endpoint names; unmapped ones are listed, not guessed.
winter_openings.rule: Open n circuits of the direct branch(es) between the two mapped buses: a branch with c circuits keeps c - n (removed if 0). Only a direct branch counts; no path search.

generators._comment: Day 7 rules, fixed 18 Nov 2026 before the generator list was built and before any solve. Reasons in day7/generator_rules.md.
generators.plant_list: IGCEP 2025-35 R2 Annex B-1(i), NGC existing installed capacity as of Nov 2024 (PDF pp.149-153).

excluded.K-Electric plants (B-1(ii)): TSEP models KE as a net export load from NTDC (I2: 2,050 / 1,001 MW). KE's own plants serve KE's internal load, which is not in the model, so including them would double count.
excluded.Import from Iran (100 MW): supplies the Makran/Gwadar system, which is not connected to the national grid
excluded.dependable capacity 0: plants with IGCEP dependable 0 MW (Neelum Jehlum, out of service) get status 0

generators.exit_check: Report (a) installed MW in the model vs IGCEP NGC installed (36,424 MW) less exclusions, and (b) the binding test: located and connected summer Pmax vs the summer requirement (TSEP load 27,097 + KE 2,050 + losses 1,033 + dcline loss), by region. Any unlocated plant blocks Day 9 until it is placed; it is not silently dropped. (The 14-day plan said NGC + KE; KE is excluded under the KE-as-export convention.)

snapshot_hours.summer_peak: evening after sunset (assumption; TSEP gives no hour). Recent NTDC summer peaks occur after sunset as rooftop solar shaves the afternoon.
snapshot_hours.winter_offpeak: night (assumption; TSEP gives no hour). TSEP notes minimum demand is lower than expected, which net-metered solar could move to midday; not modelled.

summer_peak.bagasse_note: outside the sugar crushing season (about Nov-Mar) [VERIFY]

winter_offpeak.hydro_source: January 2025 hydel generation 866 GWh (ProPakistani 20 Feb 2025, citing Arif Habib Ltd) = 1,164 MW average, divided by NGC hydro dependable 10,334 MW (WAPDA 8,237 + IPP 2,097)
winter_offpeak.wind_note: assumption, no source: January wind is weak in the Gharo-Jhimpir corridor

pmin_fraction.source: Microsoft GridSFM US data pipeline (arXiv 2605.04289 s3.4): 50 % nuclear, 30 % coal, 20 % gas CCGT, 0 % GT/renewables

reactive.qmin_note: synchronous machines absorb 50 % of Qmax (midpoint of the pipeline's 40-60 %); inverter-based (wind, solar) symmetric
reactive.source: Microsoft GridSFM US data pipeline (arXiv 2605.04289 s3.4)

cost.c1_thermal: IGCEP Annex B-2 (USD): c1 [$/MWh] = fuel cost [$/GJ] x heat rate [GJ/MWh] + variable O&M [$/MWh]. Plants with two tranches use the first (lower) tranche.
cost.fallback_source: Microsoft GridSFM pipeline fallback table (arXiv 2605.04289 Table 13); bagasse 0 as take-or-pay (research notes)
cost.currency_note: B-2 is already in USD, so no exchange rate is needed; the gate's dated-rate line is not used.

connection.location: OSM power=plant (or a substation named for the plant) found by name; the name crosswalk is logged with its basis in day7/plant_crosswalk.csv
connection.documented_voltage: Where a document names the connection voltage, it is used: PSS 44th line tables (500 kV: CFPP/Sahiwal, QATPL/Bhikki, H.B.Shah/Haveli, HUBCO, CPHGC/China HUBCO, Engro Thar, Port Qasim, Tarbela, Ghazi Barotha, Guddu 747, Neelum Jhelum; 220 kV: Chashnupp, KAPCO, Lalpir, Pak Gen, PARCO, Mangla, Allai Khawar) and TSEP Figure 5-9 plant labels on the 500 kV network.
connection.bus_rule: Otherwise: among main-component substation/plant/converter buses within 5 km of the OSM location, take the highest voltage (ties: nearest). Plants under 50 MW may use 66 kV. If none within 5 km, the nearest such bus within 20 km at any voltage >= 66 kV, with the distance logged.
connection.size_check: Flag (never silently change) any plant of >= 500 MW below 220 kV and any of >= 1,000 MW not at 500 kV; each flag is resolved in the crosswalk with its basis.
connection.unlocated: listed with MW; they block Day 9 until placed (GEM GIPT coordinates, which Furqan has to download, or a documented location)
connection.amendment_18nov: Day 7b, 18 Nov 2026, before any solve: GEM tracker coordinates placed 13 of the 18 (location 'GEM:lat,lon' in the crosswalk). The remaining 5 small hydro plants (Dargai 20, Jabban 22, Ranolia 17, Gomal Zam 17, Chitral 1 = 77 MW dependable, 0.2 % of NGC) have no OSM or GEM location, or no bus within 20 km. They are excluded with that reason and counted as missing in S2; they no longer block Day 9.

slack.summer_peak: Tarbela (largest hydro, as in the 14-day plan)
slack.winter_offpeak: bus of the largest-Pmax generator in that snapshot

generators.ke_box_generators: Declared 18 Nov 2026, before any load is placed: NGC plants (IGCEP B-1(i)) on buses that the Day 4 geometric K-Electric box flags (Dawood, FWEL-I, FWEL-II, Tenaga, Zephyr: 250 MW of Gharo wind on 220 kV) stay as NGC generators. The KE flag affects only S1's without-KE count and the Day 8 KE export placement, which uses the Day 4 interface buses only; no KE internal load is placed on these buses. The box is not moved.

buses.source: TSEP 2024-34 planning criteria (grid code), normal operating conditions: voltage within +8 % / -5 % for nominal voltages up to 500 kV. Contingency band +/-10 % is not used for the base cases.

dcline._comment: Matiari-Lahore +/-660 kV LCC bipole, 4,000 MW (NEPRA tariff revision, Business Recorder 10 Mar 2018), 887 km in the build.
dcline.setpoint_rule: Transfer is FIXED at the snapshot set-point (pmin = pmax = set-point). Summer 4,000 MW: TSEP p.34 text (input I3). Winter off-peak 2,000 MW: TSEP Figure 5-9 annotation 'Power Flow on Matiari-Lahore HVDC Link = 2000 MW' (PDF p.70), added to I3.
dcline.loss_note: NTDC-reported actual T&T loss on the PMLTC HVDC line, Nov 2024: 19.528 GWh = 3.391 % (Express Tribune, 8 Jan 2025); NEPRA allows actual losses up to 4.3 % (Business Recorder, 10 Mar 2018). Linear in transfer, no fixed term; the November figure is at partial loading, so the split between fixed and variable loss is unknown.
dcline.q_note: LCC terminals with switched filters: small net exchange assumed (+/-5 % of rating); assumption
